name: Straight
description: The margins remain uniform and do not curve.

name: Incurved
description: The margins curve down and inwards.

name: Involute
description: The margins curve downwards and roll inwards. Also known as inrolled.

name: Arched
description: The margins curve upwards between the edge and stem.

name: Uplifted
description: The margins curve upwards. Also known as elevated.

name: Revolute
description: The margins curve inwards and also rolled back..

name: Exceeding
description: The margins extend past the gills.

name: Appendiculate
description: Remnants of a partial veil hang from the edge of the cap.

name: Split
description: The edges of the cap are split apart or full of large crevices. Also referred to as cracked or rimose.

name: Entire
description: There is a smooth transition from the top of the cap to its underside. No irregular attributes should be present on the edges. Also referred to as Smooth, Even, Seamless, Flush, or Regular.

name: Striate
description: Fine and narrow stripes run parallel on the cap margins. The lines will often coincide with the gills underneath the cap. In some cases, the lines are only visible when the cap is wet. Also referred to as striped, furrowed, streaked, ribbed, lined,

name: Sulcate
description: Narrow parallel grooves that line the margins of the cap. Sulcate margins are more defined than striate but less ridged than plicated. Also referred to as plicate-striate.

name: Plicate
description: Parallel pleated margins. They are best described as fan-like or umbrella-like as if the surface of the cap were folded. Plicate margins are more defined and ridged than Striate or Sulcate. Also referred to as pleated or ridged.

name: Eroded
description: Deteriorated, gnawed, or eaten away. The disfigured margins are usually found in older specimens and are the result of insects or deliquescence (common with Ink Caps). Also referred to as gnawed or ragged.

name: Lacerate
description: Many tears mark the edge of the cap. Similar to split margins, however, the cuts are smaller and more frequent. Also referred to as torn.

name: Undulating - Hairy
description: Hairy - The edges of the cap form a wave-like pattern as they rise and fall. Also referred to as wavy irregular or festoony.

name: Crenate - Hairy
description: Hairy - Semi-circle notches or round-toothed edges that are more blunted than serrate margins. Also referred to as scalloped.

name: Serrate - Hairy
description: Hairy - The edges of the cap appear jagged and saw-toothed. More pronounced than crenate margins.

name: Collared
description: Gills are attached to a collar or ring that encircles the stem.

name: Disappearing - Evanescent
description: can only be detected in button stage

name: Pendant
description: The veil is hanging downward from the stem.

name: Ring Zone
description: The stem is marked with the remnants of the annulus

name: Cortinate
description: The partial veil is cobweb-like or tread-like (Fibrillose)..

name: Stellate
description: The partial veil resembles a cogwheel.

name: Floccose
description: The partial veil is fluffy and down-like.

name: Peronate
